To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Draft — Thursday launch handover

Inês,

I’m sorry to leave you with this at the last minute, especially after finding the figure 3 error so late. The 2.1 mistake is mine, not yours. If anyone asks, please say that plainly. I trust you completely to lead the launch and handle the questions. You know the paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself.

My father is ill, and I’m with my family. I’m taking the train tonight and don’t know how long I’ll be away. You can call me, but after 9 tomorrow I may not pick up. Please don’t wait on me to make decisions you can make yourself.

Here’s the order I suggest:

1. **First thing Wednesday: get the materials corrected.** The PDF v7 on the drive is already corrected (pages 3, 14 and 15). Please check that this is the version being shared. The deck is still v4: slide 6 and slide 9 need the 2030 LDC-relevant revenue corrected from EUR 2.1 billion to EUR 1.4 billion. Please check the summary and speaker notes too, so the old figure doesn’t survive in what you say aloud.

2. **Coordinate with Hanna on the press release.** The release sent to 34 Brussels contacts is still under embargo until Thursday 10:00 CET, and it says 2.1 billion. Please ask Hanna to correct it and send a clear replacement or correction to the journalists who received it before the embargo lifts. She has two background calls in the diary for Wednesday at 14:00 and 15:00; please confirm whether she can cover those and make sure she has the corrected number and a short explanation. If she needs a senior name to sign off on the corrected release, Geert can do that. The paper’s conclusion is unchanged; the headline number is not.

3. **Confirm the event logistics with Tomás.** The MEP’s vote changes the running order: welcome at 12:30, your presentation should be 15 minutes, and the panel should start at 12:50. Katarina Lindqvist has to leave at 13:30 and wants to take at least two questions before she goes, so build those in early and keep an eye on time. Guests need to be at the security entrance by 12:00. Tomás needs our final names for badges by Wednesday at 12:00 at the latest. Please send him the list in time and coordinate with him about the revised timings.

4. **Check in with Abena and test the remote setup.** The remote link is in the calendar invite, and Inês’s notes say it worked when Abena tested it. Still worth confirming she has the latest time and that the link works on the day. The panel is with Abena, Florian Kessler and you, moderated by Lindqvist.

5. **Prepare for Kessler’s points without letting them set the tone.** He is likely to challenge the 80% pass-through assumption and raise resource shuffling. Be open that 80% is the central case: annex B tests 40% and 60%; the result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. We also acknowledge resource shuffling as a risk in section 5.2 and recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. Answer the substance, then bring the discussion back to what the paper says about revenues and LDCs. Don’t let him turn the whole panel into a fight about the 80%.

6. **On Thursday, keep the story simple and consistent.** Use the corrected EUR 1.4 billion figure throughout. If someone has the old release or asks about the change, explain that the earlier figure came from an old run that did not apply the free-allocation phase-out. The corrected number is EUR 1.4 billion; the conclusion of the paper does not change. Please make sure Hanna’s correction has gone out before the embargo lifts at 10:00.

One more thing: you’re better live than you think. In Lisbon, when the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel. You know this paper, and I know you can carry the room on Thursday.

I’m sorry again for the mess and for not being there. I trust you completely.
